findings.evidence: The new pre-copy guard rejects symlinked Mix/Hex roots, unlisted directories and nonempty HEX_HOME. Post collection still calls tree(hex_home), which records only regular-file paths/hashes. It records no directories, no root real path/type, and merely resolves directory symlinks without adding them to the returned map. For an initially empty HEX_HOME, adding an unlisted empty directory or replacing the root with a symlink to an empty external directory produces the same empty map. hex_inventory_match remains true, so the new before/after guard cannot enforce the reviewed complete owned-directory identity after the command. The same file-only collector representation also omits empty tool directories.
findings.required_change: Have the post inventory preserve and validate root/ancestor ownership and every file/directory/symlink entry, including empty directories. Require HEX_HOME itself to remain the same real owned directory and empty after execution. Apply the complete inventory to the owned Mix/tool root, retaining precise failure evidence without deleting unknown files.
findings.title: Post-run Hex inventory does not bind directories or the owned root identity

findings.evidence: Repair2 correctly wraps protected/source/build/tool/Hex/peer post operations and record parsing with separate error capture. Final receipt construction still evaluates collector_sha256 = sha(Path(__file__)) outside collect(). The collector source is itself a frozen input. If it is unavailable after execution, protected() records the missing-input error and all other collections can finish, but this final unguarded read raises before save(name.json). The actual code from process.wait is then absent from the final receipt, reproducing the retained failure-preservation gap for a required missing-file identity case. AST inspection independently confirms this is a direct sha call in the receipt dictionary, not a guarded operation.
findings.required_change: Capture the collector and any other required final metadata/log identity reads through the independent post collector, retaining null/error values where unavailable. Construct the final receipt from already captured data and preserve the actual process exit plus distinct post failures. Final receipt writing must not depend on rereading an input already diagnosed missing.
findings.title: An unguarded collector hash can still suppress the actual-exit receipt
